chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Hafs ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not repel the beggar, even if it is with a burnt hoof.'
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum one should give to a beggar according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kulayni’s *Al-Kafi*, this hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on *sabr* (patience) and dignity in charity, teaching that even a trivial gift like a 'burnt hoof' is superior to a dismissive gesture that might humiliate the supplicant. It serves as a practical guideline for maintaining the social dignity of the poor, ensuring that the act of giving does not become a source of shame. This principle aligns with the broader Islamic ethic of *ihsan* (excellence in conduct) towards the needy.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from his father, form Haroun Bin Al Jahm, from Hafs Bin Umar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not repel the beggar, (give something) even though it be a burnt hoof’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from his father from Harun ibn al-Jahm from Hafs ibn ‘Umar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘You must not turn away one asking for help. Give him something, even if it is a burned cloven hoof (even if it is something of very little value).”’
